facts.label: Relativa sem pronome
facts.sub: Com pronome objeto, omita that: a song everybody knows, the band we heard. Com sujeito, mantenha who/that: a singer who sings well.

facts.label: Relativa sem that
facts.sub: Quando o pronome é objeto, ele pode ser omitido: a song everybody knows, the band we heard, the singer you like. Isso deixa a frase mais curta e natural.

facts.label: Quando manter o pronome
facts.sub: Se o pronome for sujeito, mantenha: a singer who sings well, a man who plays the guitar. Teste: depois do pronome vem um verbo? Então o pronome fica.

compare.br: No Brasil, dizemos “uma música que todo mundo conhece” e “a banda de que gosto”.
compare.us: Em inglês, quando o pronome é objeto, podemos cortar that: a song everybody knows, the band we heard, the singer you like. Se for sujeito, o pronome fica: a boy who plays.

pages.title: Mito ou fato? · 1/2

items.s: We can say “a song everybody knows”.
We say “a song what everybody knows”.
items.why: We say a song that everybody knows, or a song everybody knows.

items.s: We can leave out that when it is the object.

pages.instruction: Decida e explique com suas palavras.

solo: Aluno responde e justifica; você mostra a pista.
group: Cada aluno decide sozinho, depois compare as respostas e peça uma justificativa.
Corrija pela pista do texto, não só dizendo “certo/errado”.
extra90: Peça que cada aluno invente uma pergunta igual para o colega.
answers: We can say “a song everybody knows”. → Verdadeiro (Yes.)
We say “a song what everybody knows”. → Falso (We say a song that everybody knows, or a song everybody knows.)
We can leave out that when it is the object. → Verdadeiro (Yes: the band we heard.)

pages.title: A park in Atlanta · 1/3
paragraphs: It is a sunny Sunday in Atlanta. Bia and Dale listen to a song in a park. A small speaker plays an old hit. People nearby start to hum. Dale has just come back from a concert. Bia loves to talk about music.

“Bia, listen. That’s a song everybody knows.” says Dale. “Of course! It’s the song my grandfather sings in the car.” says Bia. “The singer you like plays it at every concert. I saw her last summer.” says Dale.
